0.0.n: This is the beginning of the name もなみ, not the particle も.

0.1.n: This completes the name もなみ; it is not a separate word here.

0.2.n: ちゃん follows Monami’s name to show affection or familiarity, often when addressing a child.

1.0.n: 今 tells us when the cooking is happening.

1.1.n: してる is casual している, showing an ongoing action; お adds a polite touch to 料理.

1.2.n: から follows the cooking statement to give the reason for the warning.

1.3.n: This adjective forms the warning without needing an extra word for is.

1.4.n: よ draws attention to the warning, and ー stretches the final sound.

0.tip: Read もなみ as one name despite the split; ちゃん adds affection.

1.lit: Now, cooking, so dangerous, I tell you.
1.tip: から links the reason to the warning: because I’m cooking, it’s dangerous.
